subject: Operator separation & sidecar escrow model for BYOK deployment

Subject: Request: operator separation & escrow model for BYOK sidecar

Hi Sofia / Vivek,

Thanks for taking this on. Our security and procurement teams are reviewing Redwood's private BYOK options for our upcoming on-prem deployment. Two things we need clear operational descriptions and evidentiary artifacts for:

1) Operator separation: we need to understand the exact separation of duties between operators who manage the infrastructure vs. operators who could potentially access key material. Specifically: which components (sidecar, operator VM, bastion) can ever access unwrapped key material; where are KEKs and DEKs kept; and how operator privileges are constrained in normal and recovery flows.

2) Escrow / handoff model: procurement wants an escrow fallback that doesn't allow Redwood staff to unilaterally unwrap customer keys. We're open to multi-sig escrow or escrow held by a neutral custodian. Please identify the recommended pattern and provide a proposed list of technical controls and an evidence package we can send to our auditors.

Can you share an architecture note, a short matrix of responsibilities, and any diagrams? We hope to close on these controls before vendor approval next quarter.

Thanks,

Jordan — thanks for the clear ask. High-level summary below and I've attached a short matrix and diagram.

Attachments: operator_separation_matrix.xlsx (roles & ACLs), kek_rotation_diagram.png (KEK lifecycle), escrow-draft-terms.pdf (procurement-facing draft)

Executive summary (short):
- Pattern we recommend: sidecar-based KMS proxy + customer BYOK (wrapped DEKs) + hardware-backed KEK held in customer HSM where possible.
- Operator separation: Redwood operators manage orchestration (scaling, OS patching) but never hold DEK unwrapping capability. The unwrapping happens in a customer-controlled HSM or an HSM held by an approved escrow custodian; operator workflows use attestation tokens to request wrapped tokens only.
- Escrow: dual-party escrow recommended — customer primary custodian + neutral escrow agent (e.g., third-party custodian). Escrow retrieval requires two independent approvals and an auditable request with time-limited one-time keys.

Key controls we include in the attached matrix:
- No human operators with unbounded unwrapping permissions (RBAC mapped to role IDs).
- Ephemeral sidecar keys: sidecar receives ephemeral session keys via attested channel; these keys are rotated frequently and never persisted outside memory.
- Remote attestation + TPM attestation policy for sidecar image before giving key material.
- Network segregation: KMS endpoint only accessible from VPC subnet where inference nodes run; operator jump hosts isolated to management VPC with one-way proxies.
- Automated rotation: KEK rotation runbooks + automation with canary verification against a small prompt set; results posted to an auditable log stream.

Open questions I flagged for internal follow-up (will loop in legal/procurement):
- Would you prefer escrow to be a Redwood-offered escrow service or a neutral third-party custodian?
- Do you require Redwood personnel to be excluded from the escrow workflow entirely (i.e., we cannot be signers for any recovery event)?

Propose a 30–45 minute call to walk through the matrix and confirm procurement requirements. I'm available tomorrow or Thursday afternoon PT.

— Sofia

Jordan / team — adding a few operational constraints from the runtime side:

- Sidecar design: keep sidecar process as thin as possible (no persistent disk writes of key material). We recommend a dedicated PSG (process security group) and kernel lockdown (seccomp) for the sidecar container.
- Network: dedicate a KMS subnet behind a private NLB; enforce egress allow-listing to only approved token issuers and the escrow custodian endpoints. No public egress from inference subnets.
- Attestation & logs: require platform attestation (TPM/SEV) before a node receives session DEKs. Maintain an append-only ledger (signed log stream) of attestation events and key issuance — this ledger can be exported to customer SIEM.
- Rotation: make KEK rotation asynchronous but testable: introduce canary path that validates one small production weight model before rolling to the fleet. We can automate rollback when regressions are detected.

I'll prep a short runbook excerpt we can share with procurement showing the sequence of automated events and human approvals (if any).

— Vivek
VP, Platform Engineering, Redwood Inference
